title: Clean up a repeating job
summary: disconnectedCallback runs when a custom element leaves the document.

Explain the example for clean up a repeating job

blocks.text: disconnectedCallback runs when a custom element leaves the document. Use it to stop repeating work that should no longer run.
Run these HTML examples in this site's HTML playground. Each example defines its own custom element in a fresh page. No extra JavaScript library is needed.

blocks.code:
<tick-note></tick-note>
<script>
  class TickNote extends HTMLElement {
    connectedCallback() { this.count = 0; this.timer = setInterval(() => { this.textContent = String(++this.count); }, 1000); }
    disconnectedCallback() { clearInterval(this.timer); }
  }
  customElements.define("tick-note", TickNote);
</script>
blocks.title: Clean up a repeating job

blocks.text: Read the code step by step

items: `textContent` reads or replaces plain text inside an element. It does not interpret the supplied words as HTML.
`customElements.define` registers a hyphenated tag name with its class. Register a given name only once per document.
`connectedCallback` runs when the element joins the document. It can run again after a removal and reconnection.

blocks.text: The number grows once per second. Removing the element stops its timer.

blocks.title: A mistake to avoid
blocks.text: Leaving a timer running after removal wastes work. Reconnection should start a fresh timer without leaving an old one behind.

blocks.title: Your small task
blocks.text: Remove the element after a few seconds and explain the cleanup.
